seo.title: FAQ — IDP Companion: Honest Answers About Multilingual Driver License Translation
seo.description: Everything we get asked about IDP Companion — what it is, what it isn't, how it works, where it helps, and the rental-desk situations where you'll need a government IDP instead. 28 honest answers.

hero.lead: Everything we get asked about IDP Companion — what it is, how it works, where it helps, and (just as importantly) where it doesn't. Organized so you can find what you need.

product.heading: What is IDP Companion?
product.lead: The product in plain terms — what it is, what it isn't, and why we built it.

whatIs.a: A multilingual digital PDF that translates your driver's license details into the 12 languages most commonly required at rental desks and police stops abroad — English, French, Spanish, German, Italian, Portuguese, Vietnamese, Russian, Arabic, Chinese, Japanese, and Thai. It's generated from a photo of your real license, not a generic template, and it's designed to be carried alongside your physical license — never as a replacement for it.

vsOfficialIdp.q: Is this the same as an official International Driving Permit?
vsOfficialIdp.a: No, and we're explicit about this everywhere on the site. An official International Driving Permit (IDP) is a government-recognised booklet issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention or the 1968 Vienna Convention by an authorised national body — in the US that's AAA and AATA; in the UK it's PayPoint outlets since March 2024 (replacing the Post Office); in Russia it's RosAvtoKlub (Russian Automobile Club); in Germany it's ADAC. IDP Companion is a private multilingual translation companion document. It serves a different purpose: it makes your license details readable at rental desks and police checkpoints in countries where your home license doesn't translate cleanly — without claiming to be a government IDP.

whyExists.q: Why does this product exist if official IDPs are available?
whyExists.a: Two reasons. First — getting an official IDP often requires a trip to a physical office, a passport-style photo, and 1–14 days of processing. None of which works for the traveller who realised at the airport that their UK photocard might not be enough at the rental desk in Bali. Second — for many destinations the official IDP isn't legally required, but a multilingual translation document is still operationally useful: at smaller rental agencies, at rural police checkpoints, and at any interaction where the agent's English is limited. IDP Companion is designed for those situations: $35 in 2 minutes online, valid wherever you find yourself needing to explain what your home license says.

whoNeedsIt.a: Travellers driving in countries where a translation document is either legally recommended (most non-EU destinations from a UK or US license) or operationally useful (smaller rental agencies, rural police checkpoints, off-the-tourist-path itineraries). Also: travellers combining multiple destinations on one trip — a single purchase covers them all. Also: holders of older paper licences, where rental agencies often require supplementary documentation regardless of the legal recognition position.

legitVsScammy.q: How is this different from sites that look like government IDP issuers?
legitVsScammy.a: Several scam-adjacent sites mimic government issuer branding and charge $40–80 for documents that look like official IDPs but aren't. We don't do that. We don't use government seals we don't have, we don't claim our document is an official IDP, and every destination page on this site openly states what the document is and isn't. If you need a government IDP for a destination that legally requires one (Japan, Thailand, parts of South America), we tell you where to get one from the authorised national issuer. If you need a translation companion for the broader range of situations where it actually helps, that's what we sell.

howItWorks.heading: How does it work?
howItWorks.lead: From application to printable PDF in about 2 minutes. Here's what happens behind the scenes.

howToApply.q: How do I apply for IDP Companion?
howToApply.a: Three steps. (1) Pick your origin country and plan length (1, 3, or 5 years) on the landing or pricing page. (2) Complete the application: upload a photo of your driver's license, take a headshot photo (used for face verification only), confirm a few details. (3) Pay $35–55 by card (Visa/MasterCard/Amex), PayPal, Apple Pay, or USDT/USDC/BTC/ETH — and download your PDF immediately. Total time end to end: about 2 minutes.

ocrVerification.q: What happens to my license photo?
ocrVerification.a: Your license photo runs through our OCR (optical character recognition) verification step. The OCR confirms the photo is a real driver's license, extracts the issuing country and license class, and flags low-quality or non-license images for retry. The photo is stored on our servers for 1 hour after submission and then automatically deleted — long enough to complete the application across a payment retry or browser refresh, not long enough to be a privacy concern. We do not share or sell license images.

faceMatch.q: Why do I need a headshot photo?
faceMatch.a: The headshot is used for face verification against your license photo. This is a fraud-prevention step that confirms the license belongs to the person applying. We use AWS Rekognition for the face match — your headshot is processed once at submission and discarded immediately afterwards. We do not retain face data, we do not build a face database, and we do not use the photo for anything beyond the single verification check.

deliveryTime.q: How long until I receive my IDP Companion?
deliveryTime.a: About 2 minutes from start to delivery, assuming a clean license photo and successful payment. The PDF is generated on-demand at the moment payment completes — you download it directly in the same session. There's no waiting list, no manual review queue, no email back-and-forth. The document arrives in the same browser tab you applied from.

fileFormat.q: What format is the PDF and how do I use it?
fileFormat.a: A standard PDF (~150 KB) presenting your license data on a single page in 12 languages. Print it at home on A4 or US Letter, fold it like the document it's modeled on, and carry it alongside your physical license. You can also keep it on your phone as a backup reference, but the printed version is what you'll typically hand over at rental desks and police checkpoints. The PDF is re-downloadable from your purchase receipt at any time during your plan's validity.

pricing.heading: Pricing & payment
pricing.lead: What you pay, why these plans exist, and how the payment side works.

whichPlan.q: Which plan should I pick — 1, 3, or 5 years?
whichPlan.a: If you have a single trip planned within the next year, pick 1 year ($35). If you travel internationally regularly or have multiple trips lined up, the 3-year plan ($45, about $15 per year) is the most common choice. The 5-year plan ($55, about $11 per year) is best if your driver's license has more than 5 years left until expiry and you expect to travel internationally throughout. The plan's validity is tied to your home country license — if your license expires, the companion expires with it.

whatsIncluded.a: The same PDF, the same 12-language translation, the same instant delivery. The only difference between plans is validity duration. Every plan includes: unlimited PDF re-downloads for the validity period, free regeneration if your license details change (e.g., licence renewal, name change), and multi-country coverage on a single document — one purchase works for any destination where the document applies.

paymentMethods.a: Two options. (1) Card and wallet payments via Gumroad — credit card, debit card, PayPal, and Apple Pay. (2) Cryptocurrency via NOWPayments — USDT, USDC, BTC, and ETH. Both options are live today. Card payments are processed in USD; your card issuer handles the currency conversion at the standard interbank rate. Crypto payments are settled at the network rate at the time of confirmation.

refunds.a: Full refund within 14 days of purchase if you haven't downloaded the PDF, no questions asked. After the PDF has been downloaded, we evaluate refund requests case-by-case — if there's a genuine technical issue or documentation problem on our end, we refund. We don't refund for outcomes we warned about in advance on the destination's dedicated page (e.g., 'the rental agency required a government IDP — but on the page for that destination we said upfront a government IDP was legally required there'). Email support{'@'}idpcompanion.com to start a refund.

multipleDrivers.q: Can multiple drivers share one IDP Companion?
multipleDrivers.a: No — each IDP Companion is generated from a specific person's driver's license and includes that person's name, license number, and verified photograph. If two people will both drive on the same trip, each needs their own. We don't currently offer family or multi-license discounts.

whereItWorks.heading: Where it works (and where it doesn't)
whereItWorks.lead: Honest geography of where IDP Companion is useful, where it isn't enough, and when you genuinely need a government-issued IDP.

genevaVsVienna.q: What's the difference between the 1949 Geneva and 1968 Vienna Conventions?
genevaVsVienna.a: Both are international treaties governing road traffic that recognise official government IDPs. The 1949 Geneva Convention (signed by ~100 countries including the US, UK, Australia, Japan, Thailand) is the older framework. The 1968 Vienna Convention (signed by ~85 countries including Russia, Germany, France, Brazil) is the more modern one. Some countries signed both; some only one. IDP Companion is not an official IDP under either convention — it's a translation companion that supplements your home license at rental desks and checkpoints, regardless of which convention applies to your destination.

supportedCountries.q: In which countries is IDP Companion useful?
supportedCountries.a: It's useful anywhere your driver's license is in a language the local officer or rental agent might not read fluently. That's most non-EU destinations from a UK or US license, most non-Russian-speaking countries from a Russian license, and similar combinations for other origins. Our destination pages (e.g., UK → Thailand, US → Mexico, Russia → Turkey) cover the specific legal situation, fines, and rental landscape for popular routes. If your destination is listed there, the page tells you exactly when IDP Companion helps and when you need something else.

whenNeedOfficial.q: When do I need an official government IDP instead?
whenNeedOfficial.a: When the destination's law explicitly requires a 1949 Geneva or 1968 Vienna Convention IDP and the rental agency or local police won't accept a translation companion as a substitute. Specific examples: Japan legally requires a 1949 Geneva IDP issued by an authorised home-country body for non-Japanese-license holders. Thailand legally requires an IDP for foreign tourist drivers. China generally doesn't recognise any foreign license including IDPs. If your destination requires an official IDP, get one from your country's authorised national issuer — in the US that's AAA or AATA; in the UK it's PayPoint outlets (since March 2024); in Russia it's RosAvtoKlub (Russian Automobile Club); in Germany it's ADAC. Our destination pages flag this explicitly for every destination we cover.

rentalVariance.q: Will every rental agency accept IDP Companion?
rentalVariance.a: Major international chains (Hertz, Avis, Sixt, Europcar, Budget) accept it at most airport branches across destinations where the document applies. Smaller local agencies vary — some require an official government IDP regardless of your home license. The rental conditions you agreed to at booking are the authoritative source: if they require an IDP and you arrived with only a translation companion, the agency's policy stands. Our destination pages document agency-by-agency policies for popular destinations.

ifRejected.q: What happens if a rental agency refuses to accept it?
ifRejected.a: Two scenarios. (1) The agency requires a government IDP that we explicitly told you about on the destination page (e.g., Japan, Thailand) — in that case the document isn't at fault, the legal requirement is, and we don't refund for outcomes we documented upfront. (2) The agency claims it doesn't recognise IDP Companion despite your destination not requiring a government IDP — email support{'@'}idpcompanion.com with the agency name and location, and we'll work with you on next steps including potential refund. We track agency-acceptance reports to keep our destination pages accurate.

privacy.heading: Privacy & security
privacy.lead: What data we collect, how long we keep it, and what we never do with it.

dataStorage.a: Our servers are hosted in the European Union (Frankfurt region). All data is encrypted in transit (TLS 1.3) and at rest. We use Gumroad (cards, PayPal, Apple Pay) and NOWPayments (crypto) for payment processing — payment card and wallet data never touch our servers. Personal data is handled in compliance with GDPR principles regardless of your origin country.

licensePhotoRetention.q: How long do you keep my license photo?
licensePhotoRetention.a: License photos are deleted automatically 1 hour after submission. This is a hard automated rule, not a discretionary policy. The 1-hour window exists so that if your application is interrupted (browser crash, payment retry, etc.), you can resume without re-uploading. Beyond that window the photo is gone from our systems. We never store license photos beyond the application session.

headshotUse.q: What about the headshot photo — do you keep that?
headshotUse.a: The headshot runs through AWS Rekognition for one-time face verification against your license photo and is then discarded. We don't retain face data, we don't build a face database, and we don't use the headshot for anything beyond the single verification check at submission. The headshot is also stored on our servers for at most 1 hour to handle payment retries, then deleted.

gdpr.a: Yes. We process minimal personal data, store it in the EU, use it only for the purpose you provided it for (generating your IDP Companion), and offer a documented right-to-deletion process. Email support{'@'}idpcompanion.com to request data export or deletion. Our privacy policy is the authoritative document — see /privacy-policy.

practical.heading: Practical situations
practical.lead: Edge cases, lost documents, trip changes, and the questions that come up mid-trip.

lostOrDamaged.q: What if I lose my IDP Companion or my physical license abroad?
lostOrDamaged.a: For IDP Companion: re-download it from your original purchase receipt email at any time during your plan's validity. The PDF is regenerated on-demand and you can print a fresh copy from any hotel printer or print shop. For your physical license: contact the licence-issuing authority of your home country (DVLA for UK, DMV/RMV for US, ГИБДД for Russia) — IDP Companion alone is not a substitute for your physical license, and rental agencies and police will require the original.

tripExtension.q: What if my trip extends beyond my plan's validity?
tripExtension.a: If your IDP Companion expires mid-trip, you can purchase a new one online from anywhere with internet access. The new PDF is delivered in the same ~2 minutes. If your destination's rental agency requires a continuously-valid document across the renewal date, time your purchase before the expiry date and carry both PDFs printed for the overlap day.

multipleCountries.q: Can I use one purchase for multiple countries on the same trip?
multipleCountries.a: Yes. One IDP Companion is valid wherever the document is useful — there's no per-country fee. A 5-year plan covers as many trips and destinations as you take during that period. The validity is tied to your home country license, not to specific countries or trips.

licenseExpiry.q: What if my home license expires during my IDP Companion's validity?
licenseExpiry.a: Your IDP Companion is tied to the specific driver's license you uploaded. If that license expires and you renew, the IDP Companion is no longer valid for the renewed license — you'll need to regenerate it from the new license details. Free regeneration is included in every plan. Email support{'@'}idpcompanion.com from the address you used at checkout (that's how we locate your order) with a photo of the renewed license attached. For the full breakdown of how IDP validity works under the 1949 Geneva and 1968 Vienna Conventions, see our [dedicated IDP validity guide](/idp-validity/).

cta.heading: Still have a question?
cta.text: If your question isn't covered above, we read every email. The fastest answer often comes from starting the application — most ambiguities resolve during the 2-minute process. For everything else, send us a note.

seo.title: How IDP Companion Works — 5 Steps, ~2 Minutes, Transparent Verification
seo.description: From license photo to ready-to-print PDF in about 2 minutes. Honest walkthrough of all 5 steps, including OCR + face verification, data retention rules, and realistic timing per step.

hero.lead: Five steps online, about two minutes end to end, transparent verification at every stage. Below — what each step does, what happens behind the scenes, and where your data goes after.

stepsSection.heading: From license photo to ready-to-print PDF
stepsSection.lead: Five steps, all online, ~2 minutes total. Each step explained — including what we do with the data you upload.

pickPlan.title: Pick origin country + plan
pickPlan.summary: Choose your driver's license country of issue and the plan length — 1, 3, or 5 years.
pickPlan.detail: Selecting your origin determines which license format we expect on the upload step. The plan length is purely commercial — same PDF, same translation across plans, validity tied to your home license. You can change either choice before paying.

uploadLicense.title: Upload your license photo
uploadLicense.summary: Take a phone photo or upload a scan — JPG, PNG, or PDF. Front side with the photo and license number is enough for most countries.
uploadLicense.detail: We accept any clear, in-focus image where the license fills most of the frame. The file is uploaded over TLS 1.3 to our EU servers and queued for OCR verification. No watermarks, no compression artifacts, no special equipment required — a phone photo in good light works.

selfie.title: Take a selfie
selfie.summary: We compare the selfie to the photo on your license to confirm the license belongs to you.
selfie.detail: This is the only fraud-prevention step in the flow. We don't ask for additional documents, signatures, or callbacks — the match is automated and runs in about five seconds. Glasses, lighting differences, and license-photo age usually still match; if rejected, you can retry.

pay.title: Pay by card or crypto
pay.summary: $35 (1 year), $45 (3 years), or $55 (5 years). One-time payment, no subscription.
pay.detail: Two options. Card and wallet payments via Gumroad — credit card (Visa, MasterCard, Amex), debit card, PayPal, or Apple Pay. Cryptocurrency payments via NOWPayments — USDT, USDC, BTC, and ETH. Both live today. Card payments processed in USD with your card issuer handling the currency conversion at the standard interbank rate; crypto payments settle at the network rate at the time of confirmation.

download.title: Download your PDF
download.summary: Generated instantly after payment. ~150 KB, A4 or US Letter, ready to print at home.
download.detail: The PDF is generated on-demand at the moment payment completes and downloads directly in the same browser session — no waiting list, no email back-and-forth. The receipt email also contains a re-download link valid for the duration of your plan.

verification.heading: How we verify it's actually you, and a real license
verification.lead: Two automated checks — neither involves a human reviewing your photo. Both finish in seconds, and both delete their input data within an hour.

ocr.title: OCR — confirms it's a real license
ocr.body: Optical character recognition reads the license image to confirm it's an actual driver's license, extracts the issuing country and license class, and rejects low-quality images, random photos, or non-license documents. The check runs server-side in about five seconds. If your photo is too blurry, has glare, or is at a bad angle, you can retry — up to 5 attempts per session.

face.title: Face match — confirms the license is yours
face.body: Your selfie is compared against the photo on your license using AWS Rekognition's CompareFaces API. The similarity threshold is 85% — high enough to prevent obvious fraud, low enough to accommodate glasses, age differences, and lighting. Match runs in about five seconds. If you're rejected (rare, but happens with old or low-quality license photos), retry with a better selfie.

whatYouGet.heading: What you receive
whatYouGet.lead: A single-page PDF designed to be carried alongside your physical license. Print it at home, fold it like a passport, or keep it on your phone as a backup reference.

format.title: Single-page PDF (~150 KB)
format.body: Standard PDF format, A4 or US Letter, fold-style modeled on the 1949 Geneva Convention IDP layout. Opens in any PDF reader; no special software required.

languages.title: 12 languages
languages.body: Your license data presented on one page in the 12 languages most commonly required at rental desks and police stops abroad.

usage.title: Print or phone
usage.body: Print at home, hotel, or print shop. Phone display works as a backup for in-car checks. The printed version is what you'll typically hand over at rental desks and police checkpoints.

validity.title: Re-downloadable
validity.body: Re-download anytime during your plan's validity from the purchase receipt email. Free regeneration if your license details change (renewal, name change).

timing.heading: Realistic timing — step by step
timing.lead: Average ~2 minutes end to end if your license photo is clean and payment goes through on the first try. Per-step estimates based on actual user sessions:
timing.note: Edge cases add time: failed OCR retry (~30 sec each), payment retry (~1 min), low-quality license image requiring rescan (~1–2 min). The fastest sessions complete in under 90 seconds; the longest still finish in under 5 minutes.

trust.heading: Where your data goes (and where it doesn't)
trust.lead: Four hard automated rules, applied to every application.

licensePhoto.label: License photo
licensePhoto.detail: Deleted automatically 1 hour after submission — hard automated rule, not a discretionary policy. The 1-hour window exists so you can resume an interrupted application (browser crash, payment retry) without re-uploading. Never shared, never sold.

headshot.label: Headshot selfie
headshot.detail: Used once for the face-match check, then discarded. We don't retain face data, we don't build a face database, and we don't use the photo for anything beyond the single verification at submission.

payment.label: Card data
payment.detail: Never touches our servers. Gumroad handles card and wallet checkout (PCI-DSS Level 1 compliant); NOWPayments handles crypto checkout (USDT, USDC, BTC, ETH). We never see, store, or log card numbers, wallet addresses, or seed phrases.

servers.label: Server location
servers.detail: EU (Frankfurt region). All data encrypted in transit (TLS 1.3) and at rest. GDPR-compliant regardless of your origin country. Email support{'@'}idpcompanion.com to request data export or deletion.

cta.heading: Ready to start?
cta.text: ~2 minutes online, transparent verification at every step, your data deleted within an hour. $35 / 1 year · $45 / 3 years · $55 / 5 years. One-time payment, no subscription.

seo.title: Security & Payments — How We Protect Your License Data and Card Details
seo.description: End-to-end view of how IDP Companion handles your license photo, selfie, payment data and PDF. EU servers, TLS 1.3, 1-hour deletion of biometric inputs, no card data on our servers.

hero.h1: Security & Payments — what we hold, for how long, and why
hero.lead: We built IDP Companion the way we'd want a service handling our own driver's licence to work. The licence photo and selfie are used only for verification and get deleted within an hour. We never see or store your card details. Servers are in the European Union, traffic is encrypted with TLS 1.3 on the way in, files are encrypted with AES-256 at rest. Every step is laid out below.

lifecycle.heading: Data lifecycle — what each input becomes and when it's gone
lifecycle.lead: Five things reach our servers when you order an IDP Companion: your licence photo, your selfie, the generated PDF, your payment data and your application profile. Each follows a distinct lifecycle.

licensePhoto.title: Licence photo
licensePhoto.body: Uploaded to a temporary storage area. A text-recognition engine (Tesseract OCR) reads the licence number, full name, expiry date and class from the image. Up to 5 retries if the first read fails. The image is automatically deleted within 60 minutes whether verification passed or not — no review queue, no manual archive, no backup.

headshot.title: Selfie / headshot
headshot.body: Compared with the photo on your licence using AWS Rekognition (85% similarity threshold). We do not store face templates, biometric profiles or a searchable face database. The selfie file is deleted within 60 minutes — only the pass / fail result and similarity score stay attached to your application.

pdf.title: Generated PDF
pdf.body: Built in server memory the moment you click download — never written to disk. Each download regenerates the PDF from your stored application fields, so there is no cache, no CDN copy and no backup of the rendered file.

profile.title: Application profile
profile.body: Name, date of birth, licence class and country, plan length, payment status and order ID. We need this to re-issue the PDF for the duration of your plan and to handle refunds or chargebacks. Retained until your plan expires plus twelve months (tax and audit law require it) and then removed at the next quarterly cleanup.

infra.heading: Encryption & infrastructure
infra.lead: Anything that reaches our service travels over an encrypted connection (TLS 1.3), is stored on servers inside the European Union and sits on encrypted disks. Access to the live database is limited to a couple of people, every action is logged and the access list is reviewed regularly.

inTransit.title: Protection in transit
inTransit.body: All traffic between your browser and our server uses TLS 1.3 — the modern encryption standard. Any attempt to connect over plain HTTP is immediately redirected to HTTPS.
inTransit.chip1: TLS 1.3 only — older versions are turned off
inTransit.chip2: HSTS enabled (1 year + preload) — the browser refuses insecure connections
inTransit.chip3: No mixed HTTP/HTTPS resources on any page

atRest.title: Protection at rest
atRest.body: Database fields holding personal data sit on AES-256 encrypted disks. Uploaded images stay in encrypted storage for exactly the hour they wait to be deleted.
atRest.chip1: AES-256 disk encryption for PostgreSQL volumes
atRest.chip2: Encrypted file storage for uploads (one hour, then gone)
atRest.chip3: Encryption keys live in the provider's key-management service, not in the app's code

hosting.title: EU hosting + Cloudflare
hosting.body: Application servers run inside the European Union (Frankfurt region). The static landing site is served through Cloudflare for speed, but only public images and scripts sit in that cache — no personal data ever ends up in the global distribution network.
hosting.chip2: Cloudflare only for the landing site's static assets
hosting.chip3: No personal data cached outside our own servers

access.title: Access control
access.body: Two engineers can reach the live database, and only through short-lived credentials that rotate regularly. Every connection is written to the log. No third-party tools have direct read access to the database.

payments.heading: Payment security — what reaches us and what never does
payments.lead: Card payments and crypto payments are handled end-to-end by certified payment providers (Gumroad is PCI-DSS compliant). Card numbers, CVVs and crypto wallet keys never reach our infrastructure — not even briefly in memory.

gumroad.title: Gumroad
gumroad.sub: Cards · PayPal · Apple Pay · Google Pay
gumroad.body: Gumroad is a large PCI-DSS certified payment provider that runs the whole checkout. We hand the user off with a plan reference; Gumroad collects the payment and sends us back a digitally-signed confirmation once it's done. The card details never reach us.
gumroad.leaves2: Customer email (for the receipt and PDF delivery)

nowpayments.title: NOWPayments
nowpayments.body: Crypto payments go through a hosted NOWPayments invoice page. They generate the temporary wallet, watch for the blockchain confirmation and handle the conversion. We get a digitally-signed confirmation when the transaction is verified — we never hold the wallet keys ourselves.
nowpayments.leaves2: Confirmed transaction hash on the blockchain

payments.footnote: Both providers send back digitally-signed confirmations — we can verify each message really came from them. Any notification that fails the signature check is rejected before it ever reaches our application code.

compliance.heading: Privacy & GDPR rights
compliance.lead: IDP Companion processes personal data under GDPR. Three rights from that law matter most for what we do — and we've made each of them easy to exercise: a single email is enough.

access.title: Right to know what we hold
access.body: Ask for a copy of every personal-data record we hold about you. Within 30 days we'll send a JSON or PDF export of your application profile, payment receipts and system event history.

erasure.title: Right to erasure
erasure.body: Ask for permanent deletion of your application data. We action it within 30 days. The exception: financial records that tax and audit law oblige us to keep (typically 7 years in the EU).

portability.title: Right to take your data with you
portability.body: Receive your data in a machine-readable format (JSON) so you can move it elsewhere or simply archive it. Useful if you're switching to a different translation service or keeping a personal record of your applications.

compliance.exerciseBody: Email us with the subject line below. Include the email you used at checkout. We reply within 30 days — that's the deadline GDPR Article 12(3) sets.

report.heading: Report a security issue
report.body: Spotted a vulnerability, a potential data exposure or something on the site that looks wrong? We want to hear about it. We don't run a public bug-bounty program yet, but we read every report and confirm receipt within 24 hours.

steps.step1: Email the details to the address below. Describe the issue, the steps to reproduce it and what you think the real-world impact could be.
steps.step2: We confirm receipt within 24 hours and look into it within 72 hours. We won't threaten legal action against good-faith research.
steps.step3: Critical findings get a same-day patch where it's possible. If you want public credit, we'll thank you in our changelog.

audit.heading: Trust checklist — six things we never do
audit.lead: If any of these stopped being true tomorrow, our whole security model would fall apart. That's why they are written into the code itself and verified by automated tests.

noCardData.label: We never store card details
noCardData.detail: Card numbers, CVVs and full card details don't reach our servers at all — Gumroad handles them end-to-end.

noFaceDb.label: We never build a face database
noFaceDb.detail: AWS Rekognition compares two images at the moment of the request and that's it. We don't store face templates, biometric profiles or a searchable face database.

licenseDelete.label: Licence photo deleted within 1 hour
licenseDelete.detail: Automated cleanup runs every 10 minutes. No licence photo survives the 60-minute deadline.

headshotDelete.label: Selfie deleted within 1 hour
headshotDelete.detail: Same cleanup schedule. Only the pass / fail result stays attached to your application.

euServers.label: Servers stay in the EU
euServers.detail: The database and application servers are hosted inside the European Union (Frankfurt region).

tls13.label: Encrypted everywhere, no shortcuts
tls13.detail: Plain HTTP redirects to HTTPS immediately. Older encryption versions are turned off. HSTS preload stops browsers from connecting insecurely in the first place.

cta.heading: Questions about how we protect your data?
cta.text: We reply to every privacy and security question we get. Take a look at our How-it-works page for the step-by-step view of the process, or just write to us directly.

include.lead: These details make it much quicker to sort out. Skip anything that doesn't apply to your case.

orderId.hint: You'll find it in the Gumroad or NOWPayments confirmation email — it's a 6–8 character code at the start.

visa.label: Visa, entry or immigration questions
visa.hint: Contact the embassy or consulate of the country you're travelling to. We can't assess visa eligibility.

governmentIdp.label: Getting or renewing an official government IDP
governmentIdp.hint: Contact the authorised issuer in your home country: AAA / AATA in the US, PayPoint in the UK, РОСАВТОКЛУБ in Russia, ADAC in Germany.

lostLicense.label: Replacing a lost or expired domestic licence
lostLicense.hint: That one goes to your DMV / DVLA / equivalent national authority. To create the IDP Companion we need your domestic licence to be valid.

localLaw.label: Country-specific legal advice
localLaw.hint: We publish honest destination guides but can't give legal advice. For specific questions, contact a lawyer in the destination country.
